beats.hook: A stranger tried to sell me my own stolen car — and almost got away with it.
beats.setup: My name's not important. What matters is that three weeks before this, my car vanished from a parking garage in downtown Cleveland.
beats.incident: I filed a police report. Got nowhere. So I started checking Facebook Marketplace myself. Then I saw it — my green '09 Civic, same dent above the rear wheel, listed for eighteen hundred dollars. The seller's name was "Mike T." What I couldn't figure out yet was how he knew to list it two cities away.
beats.escalation: I texted Mike. Played dumb. Asked if I could come see it in person. He said yes — gave me an address in Akron. Here's the part that still gets me: he asked me to bring cash and an ID. To buy my own car.
beats.payoff: I brought cash, alright. And two police officers. We pulled up. Mike was standing right there in the driveway — keys in hand. The officers ran the VIN before he could say a single word. It came back registered to me. Mike's face went completely white. I took my keys back on the spot.
beats.cta: He actually tried to negotiate with the cops. What would you have done — met him alone, or called it in like I did? Tell me in the comments.
